title: bug: ber_len_encode() silently truncates val > 0xFFFF
description: ber_len_encode() in wp11_proto_piv.c encodes only one-byte and two-byte BER lengths. If val > 0xFFFF, the two-byte encoding path silently writes buf[1]=(val>>8)&0xFF, buf[2]=val&0xFF -- emitting the low 16 bits only, which is decoded as a completely different (smaller) length. This truncation is silent: the function returns 3 (success) with wrong output. BER three-byte long form (0x83 prefix) is not supported. In practice PIV payloads don't exceed 0xFFFF, but a caller passing a large accumulation could corrupt APDU framing. Fix: return -1 if val > 0xFFFF.
